front: Average-case time to insert into a BST?
What input order produces a degenerate (worst-case) BST?
back: Already-sorted input — the tree becomes a linked list, O(n) operations.

front: In-order traversal of a BST visits nodes in what order?
back: Ascending sorted order of their values.

front: BST delete: a node with two children is removed by replacing it with...?
back: Its successor — the smallest key in its right subtree (found by walking left from z.right until there's no more left child).

front: Preorder traversal alone — does it uniquely determine a tree's shape?
back: No. But preorder + inorder together (with all-unique keys) do uniquely reconstruct the tree.

front: Which traversal order is naturally suited to safely deleting an entire tree?
back: Postorder (left, right, node) — children are freed before their parent.

front: What is the BST invariant for a node z?
back: Everything in z's left subtree is < z.key, everything in z's right subtree is ≥ z.key.

front: How do you tell if a sequence of numbers is a valid BST search path?
back: Going left at a node sets an upper bound for all later values; going right sets a lower bound. If any later value violates a previously-set bound, no BST could produce that path.

front: Can a BST be uniquely reconstructed from its postorder traversal alone (no inorder needed)?
back: Yes -- the last element of postorder is always the root, and the BST ordering property determines exactly where the left/right subtree split falls in the rest of the sequence.

front: Is it true that every BST with unique keys and no half-leaves can be uniquely reconstructed from inorder alone?
back: No -- false. A minimal 5-node counterexample exists: two different such BSTs share the identical inorder traversal 15,20,30,50,60.

front: BST-sort (insert all values then inorder-traverse): best-case and worst-case runtime?
back: Best case O(n log n) (tree stays balanced). Worst case Theta(n^2) (sorted input degenerates the tree into a chain).

front: Strict (full) binary tree with n nodes -- exact leaf count formula?
back: (n+1)/2 leaves, provable by induction on the recursive split into left/right strict subtrees.

front: Does a rotation (the core primitive of AVL/Red-Black/Splay trees) ever break the BST ordering property?
back: No -- provable by case analysis on every node's new left/right subtree membership after the rotation; every case preserves the original key ordering.
